question: Explain the difference between Next.js App Router (app directory) and Pages Router (pages directory).
idealAnswer: The Pages Router routes based on file paths with page-level data fetching (getServerSideProps). The App Router uses React Server Components (RSC) by default, supports nested layouts, loading/error boundaries, streaming, and Server Actions.
ideal_answer: The Pages Router routes based on file paths with page-level data fetching (getServerSideProps). The App Router uses React Server Components (RSC) by default, supports nested layouts, loading/error boundaries, streaming, and Server Actions.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Architecture and App Router vs Pages Router comprehension.

question: What are React Server Components (RSC) in Next.js, and how do they differ from Client Components ('use client')?
idealAnswer: Server Components render exclusively on the server, have direct database access, and ship zero JavaScript bundle to the browser. Client Components ('use client') render on the server and hydrate in the browser, enabling interactivity, state (useState), and event listeners.
ideal_answer: Server Components render exclusively on the server, have direct database access, and ship zero JavaScript bundle to the browser. Client Components ('use client') render on the server and hydrate in the browser, enabling interactivity, state (useState), and event listeners.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Server Components and Server Components vs Client Components comprehension.

question: Explain Server-Side Rendering (SSR), Static Site Generation (SSG), and Client-Side Rendering (CSR) in Next.js.
idealAnswer: SSR renders HTML on every incoming request (fresh data, higher TTFB). SSG generates static HTML at build time (blazing fast caching on CDN). CSR downloads empty HTML and renders on client via JS.
ideal_answer: SSR renders HTML on every incoming request (fresh data, higher TTFB). SSG generates static HTML at build time (blazing fast caching on CDN). CSR downloads empty HTML and renders on client via JS.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Rendering Strategies and SSR vs SSG vs CSR comprehension.

question: What is Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) in Next.js, and how does background revalidation work?
idealAnswer: ISR allows updating static pages in the background without rebuilding the entire website. Setting a revalidate interval serves cached static HTML immediately while regenerating fresh pages in the background when traffic arrives.
ideal_answer: ISR allows updating static pages in the background without rebuilding the entire website. Setting a revalidate interval serves cached static HTML immediately while regenerating fresh pages in the background when traffic arrives.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Rendering Strategies and Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) comprehension.

question: Explain Next.js Server Actions and how they enable secure mutations directly from client forms without dedicated API routes.
idealAnswer: Server Actions are asynchronous server functions invoked directly from client components or HTML forms (<form action={action}>). They eliminate the need to write manual API endpoints, handle form serialization, and automatically trigger cache revalidation (revalidatePath).
ideal_answer: Server Actions are asynchronous server functions invoked directly from client components or HTML forms (<form action={action}>). They eliminate the need to write manual API endpoints, handle form serialization, and automatically trigger cache revalidation (revalidatePath).
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Data Mutation and Server Actions comprehension.

question: How does Next.js Caching work across the 4 levels: Request Memoization, Data Cache, Full Route Cache, and Router Cache?
idealAnswer: Next.js manages 4 caches: Request Memoization deduplicates identical fetch() calls in a render pass; Data Cache persists fetched data across requests; Full Route Cache stores rendered HTML/RSC payloads on server; Router Cache stores RSC payloads in browser memory.
ideal_answer: Next.js manages 4 caches: Request Memoization deduplicates identical fetch() calls in a render pass; Data Cache persists fetched data across requests; Full Route Cache stores rendered HTML/RSC payloads on server; Router Cache stores RSC payloads in browser memory.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Performance & Caching and Next.js 4-Tier Caching Architecture comprehension.

question: Explain Next.js Middleware (middleware.ts), where it runs (Edge runtime), and common use cases (authentication, redirects, geolocation).
idealAnswer: Middleware runs on the Edge before a request is completed. It inspects cookies/headers, performs authentication redirects, rewrites URLs, and injects custom headers with low latency before hitting server routes.
ideal_answer: Middleware runs on the Edge before a request is completed. It inspects cookies/headers, performs authentication redirects, rewrites URLs, and injects custom headers with low latency before hitting server routes.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Routing & Middleware and Edge Middleware comprehension.

question: How does Image Optimization with the next/image component work, and what benefits does it provide over standard ?
idealAnswer: The next/image component automatically optimizes image formats (serving WebP/AVIF), resizes images dynamically for client viewports, prevents Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) via explicit dimensions, and lazily loads images offscreen.
ideal_answer: The next/image component automatically optimizes image formats (serving WebP/AVIF), resizes images dynamically for client viewports, prevents Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) via explicit dimensions, and lazily loads images offscreen.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Performance and Next.js Image Component comprehension.

question: What are Dynamic Routes, Catch-all routes ([...slug]), and Optional Catch-all routes ([[...slug]]) in Next.js?
idealAnswer: Dynamic routes ([id]) match variable URL parameters. Catch-all routes ([...slug]) match multi-level paths (e.g. /docs/a/b). Optional catch-all routes ([[...slug]]) also match the root route without parameters.
ideal_answer: Dynamic routes ([id]) match variable URL parameters. Catch-all routes ([...slug]) match multi-level paths (e.g. /docs/a/b). Optional catch-all routes ([[...slug]]) also match the root route without parameters.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Routing and Dynamic & Catch-all Routes comprehension.

question: Explain generateStaticParams in App Router and how it replaces getStaticPaths from the Pages Router.
idealAnswer: generateStaticParams generates static routes at build time for dynamic route segments ([slug]). It runs at build time to return an array of segment values, producing pre-rendered static HTML.
ideal_answer: generateStaticParams generates static routes at build time for dynamic route segments ([slug]). It runs at build time to return an array of segment values, producing pre-rendered static HTML.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Static Generation and generateStaticParams comprehension.

question: How do Route Handlers (route.ts) work in Next.js App Router for REST API endpoints (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)?
idealAnswer: Route Handlers define custom request handlers for API routes using web-standard Request and Response objects. Exporting functions named GET, POST, PUT, DELETE handles corresponding HTTP requests with full Edge/Node runtime support.
ideal_answer: Route Handlers define custom request handlers for API routes using web-standard Request and Response objects. Exporting functions named GET, POST, PUT, DELETE handles corresponding HTTP requests with full Edge/Node runtime support.

question: Explain Next.js Font Optimization with next/font and how it eliminates external network requests and layout shift.
idealAnswer: next/font automatically downloads and self-hosts Google Fonts or local fonts at build time. Fonts are served directly with the same domain assets, eliminating render-blocking external network requests and FOIT/FOUT layout shifts.
ideal_answer: next/font automatically downloads and self-hosts Google Fonts or local fonts at build time. Fonts are served directly with the same domain assets, eliminating render-blocking external network requests and FOIT/FOUT layout shifts.

question: What are Parallel Routes (@folder) and Intercepting Routes ((..)folder) in Next.js App Router?
idealAnswer: Parallel routes (@slot) allow simultaneously rendering multiple independent page slots in the same layout. Intercepting routes ((..)photo) allow loading a route inside the current context (e.g., photo modal in a feed) while preserving direct URL shareability on refresh.
ideal_answer: Parallel routes (@slot) allow simultaneously rendering multiple independent page slots in the same layout. Intercepting routes ((..)photo) allow loading a route inside the current context (e.g., photo modal in a feed) while preserving direct URL shareability on refresh.
explanation: Evaluates Next.js Advanced Routing and Parallel & Intercepting Routes comprehension.

question: How do loading.tsx, error.tsx, and not-found.tsx work as special files in Next.js App Router with React Suspense?
idealAnswer: loading.tsx automatically wraps page components in React Suspense to show instant skeleton states. error.tsx creates a React Error Boundary catching runtime errors in route segments without crashing the entire page.
